title: Agrawal S, Dickinson ES, Sustar A, et al. Central processing of leg proprioception in Drosophila (eLife; bioRxiv 10.1101/2020.06.04.132811)
why: Own CsChrimson activation of hemilineage-defined split-GAL4 populations (9Aalpha, 10Balpha, 13Balpha) in headless tethered flies (leg/joint movements) and in intact walking flies (10Balpha -> pausing; 9Aalpha no change in walking speed). Reported as screening 'a panel of hemilineage-specific split-Gal4 lines'. Populations are named subsets (alpha), so likely partial_or_mixed.

title: Syed DS, Ravbar P, Simpson JH. Inhibitory circuits control leg movements during Drosophila grooming (eLife 2026; bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.06.05.597468)
why: Own CsChrimson activation (continuous and pulsed) of 13A and 13B neurons in intact and headless adults during grooming; reported reduced grooming, static over-extension of front legs, leg locked in flexion (13B), induced grooming/walking with pulsed 13A activation. Drivers label ~6-7 13A and ~3 13B neurons per hemisegment (R35G04-DBD x GAD-AD; R35G04-DBD x Dbx-AD; R11B07-DBD x GAD-AD) = subsets. CAUTION: paper also contains a computational model; not read beyond abstract/search snippets (PROTOCOL s5).

title: Pop S, Chen CL, Sproston CJ, Kondo S, Ramdya P, Williams DW. Extensive and diverse patterns of cell death sculpt neural networks in insects (eLife; bioRxiv 10.1101/626465)
why: Own TrpA1 heat-ramp activation of 'undead' (cell-death-blocked, dronc MARCM) octopaminergic neurons of the medial neuroblast lineage (undead hemilineage 0B per search snippet) in decapitated adult males -> walking (bioRxiv v2 Fig 5B-E, Video S1). Clonal (MARCM, TDC2-GAL4), and the activated cells are normally-dying undead neurons, not a wild-type hemilineage.
hemilineages_as_named: undead hemilineage 0B (medial lineage; TDC2+ undead neurons)

title: Elabbady L, Chou GM, Sustar A, Cook A, Collman F, Tuthill JC. A central somatotopic map of the fly leg supports spatially targeted grooming (bioRxiv; also Curr Biol 2026, PMID 41966690)
why: Own CsChrimson activation of 23B interneuron subtypes (distal-sensing, e.g. R21B10; proximal-sensing; SS04746) -> targeted front/middle leg grooming with percentages. Subsets of 23B, not whole hemilineage. Journal DOI not retrieved.

title: Shirangi TR, Wong AM, Truman JW, Stern DL. Doublesex regulates the connectivity of a neural circuit controlling Drosophila male courtship song (Dev Cell 37:533-544)
why: Highlights: dsx+ TN1 neurons 'necessary and sufficient' for sine song, implying own adult activation of TN1 (a male-specific subset that other sources place in hemilineage 12A). Full text not opened; whether the paper names hemilineage 12A for its activation experiment is unverified.
hemilineages_as_named: TN1 / TN1A (12A subset; hemilineage naming unverified)

title: Ye D, Walsh JT, Junker IP, Ding Y. Changes in the cellular makeup of motor patterning circuits drive courtship song evolution in Drosophila (Curr Biol 34(11); bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.01.23.576861)
why: Own optogenetic activation of TN1 neurons in D. melanogaster/D. yakuba males (sine song and singing wing posture). TN1 is a 12A subset; abstract does not name a hemilineage. Probably does not meet the 'named hemilineage' criterion.

title: Dallmann CJ, Luo Y, Agrawal S, et al. Presynaptic inhibition selectively suppresses leg proprioception in behaving Drosophila (bioRxiv 2023; Nature 2025 10.1038/s41586-025-09554-2)
why: Search snippet says authors transiently (1 s) optogenetically activated or silenced 9A neurons in tethered flies walking on a treadmill; abstract does not mention activation. A 9A subset (hook-axon-presynaptic 9A cells). Needs full-text check of what activation produced.
